title: One performance. Many ways to shoot it.
intro: The first prototypes treated camera movement too closely as a property of each shot. That made a cut feel like a new animation task, even when it reused the same performance.

I worked toward three distinct concepts: a scene holds the performance, a camera has its own movement, and a shot chooses which camera and source interval to show. Editing the sequence should not require rebuilding the action.

blocks.label: CONCEPT MODEL · ILLUSTRATIVE 12-SECOND SCENE
blocks.caption: A → B → A reuses the same cameras and performance. Shots select intervals; they do not restart the character’s motion.

items.title: Scene = what happens.
body: Characters and props move through a shared scene timeline.

items.title: Camera = how it is filmed.
body: Each camera retains its position and orientation over time, independently of the edit.

items.title: Shot = what is shown.
body: A shot selects a camera and a source interval. Trimming or reordering changes the assembled sequence.

blocks.alt: Delivered film-preview interface showing shot thumbnails and camera keyframes
blocks.caption: Delivered product · Film Preview brings the shot sequence and camera keyframes together.

blocks.label: THE IMPORTANT TRADEOFF
blocks.text: Reusing a camera also means sharing its edits.
blocks.note: The interface needs to distinguish previewing another camera from replacing the camera used by a shot.
